status: Prepared for human review; UI states are local design simulations.

use_cases.title: Register account
use_cases.preconditions: Visitor is signed out and can reach the registration page.
use_cases.trigger: Visitor selects Create account.
steps: Visitor enters an email, password and optional display name and self-assessed CEFR level.
System validates the fields and explains that account creation grants no media or analysis consent.
Visitor submits; system normalizes email comparison and atomically creates the account and default profile.
System confirms registration and directs the visitor to sign in; no session or microphone is started.
use_cases.success: One account and its profile exist; the visitor remains signed out.
use_cases.minimum: A failed atomic write leaves neither a partial account nor a partial profile.
use_cases.special: Email at most 254 characters; password 12–128 without trimming; display name 1–80; CEFR A2/B1/B2/C1. Argon2id hashing occurs server-side. No passwords in screenshots/logs.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, optional profile values are omitted.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, optional profile values are omitted.
alternatives.outcome: System uses Learner and B1 defaults; registration may continue.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, email/password/display name/CEFR is invalid.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, email/password/display name/CEFR is invalid.
alternatives.outcome: Show field errors, retain nonsensitive fields, clear the password, and create no account.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, email already exists.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, email already exists.
alternatives.outcome: Return EMAIL_EXISTS without creating another account; offer sign-in, and recovery only when UC-01-05 is implemented and enabled.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 3, throttling or a failed/ambiguous response occurs.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, throttling or a failed/ambiguous response occurs.
alternatives.outcome: Apply Section 2.4 error handling: respect Retry-After or reconcile by sign-in before retrying; offer recovery only when UC-01-05 is implemented and enabled. Never claim success without confirmation.

use_cases.title: Sign in
use_cases.preconditions: Visitor has an account and is signed out.
use_cases.trigger: Visitor selects Sign in.
steps: Visitor enters email and password and submits once.
System validates credentials and account eligibility without revealing which check failed.
System establishes the authorized session and returns the learner identity using the explicit reduced-PA3 or full-product contract in Section 2.5.
System opens the menu or a previously requested authorized page without creating a room or requesting microphone permission.
use_cases.success: A verified session identifies the user and enables only their authorized actions.
use_cases.minimum: Failed sign-in grants no access and discloses no account eligibility details.
use_cases.special: Sections 2.4 and 2.5 define auth errors and the FR-01 session lifecycle, including renewal, expiry, replay and lost-response handling. Keep access tokens only in runtime memory; never expose server secrets. Full refresh rotation remains outside reduced PA3 implementation scope.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 4, an invite destination was preserved.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, an invite destination was preserved.
alternatives.outcome: After sign-in, reopen invite entry; joining still requires its own capacity/state checks.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, credentials are wrong, suspended or deleted.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, credentials are wrong, suspended or deleted.
alternatives.outcome: Show the same generic invalid-credentials message; issue no session.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 2, fields are malformed or login is rate limited.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, fields are malformed or login is rate limited.
alternatives.outcome: Show validation or retry timing; retain email, clear password.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 3, session creation or network confirmation fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, session creation or network confirmation fails.
alternatives.outcome: Apply Section 2.4 error handling and remain signed out until a valid login response is received; do not show a fake logged-in screen.

use_cases.title: Maintain learner profile
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated and editing their own profile; this future workflow is enabled.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Profile and chooses Edit.
steps: System loads the learner current display name, native language, CEFR and goals.
Learner changes the supported fields and reviews the self-assessment explanation.
System validates the update against the authenticated identity and saves it atomically.
System displays saved values and confirms that subsequent recommendations use them.
use_cases.success: Only permitted own-profile fields are updated.
use_cases.minimum: No other account changes; invalid requests leave the saved profile unchanged.
use_cases.special: CEFR is self-assessed, never certified. Never accept user_id, role, email or password_hash as editable profile fields.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, learner cancels or makes no changes.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, learner cancels or makes no changes.
alternatives.outcome: Leave the saved profile unchanged and return to the read view.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, fields are invalid or include identity/role changes.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, fields are invalid or include identity/role changes.
alternatives.outcome: Reject the update, show errors, and preserve the saved profile.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, identity expires or the save response is lost.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, identity expires or the save response is lost.
alternatives.outcome: Require sign-in or reload the authorized profile to reconcile; keep nonsensitive draft values until resolved.

use_cases.title: Sign out
use_cases.preconditions: An authenticated user has a browser session; the sign-out auth contract is available.
use_cases.trigger: User selects Sign out.
steps: System stops local media if any and closes private subscriptions/polling for this browser.
System submits sign-out using the current auth session and clears local credential state.
Server invalidates the session according to its auth contract and clears any session cookie.
System returns to sign-in and prevents cached private views from remaining visible.
use_cases.success: This browser is signed out; confirmed server revocation is reflected honestly.
use_cases.minimum: Local capture and private views stop even if the server cannot be reached.
use_cases.special: Do not claim all devices signed out. Back navigation must not reveal cached private data; no-store applies to private resources.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, session already expired or was revoked.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, session already expired or was revoked.
alternatives.outcome: Treat sign-out as idempotent and show the signed-out page.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, the network is unavailable.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, the network is unavailable.
alternatives.outcome: Clear local access immediately, disclose that server revocation is unconfirmed, and retry revocation when possible.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 1, a LIVE room is open.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, a LIVE room is open.
alternatives.outcome: Stop this browser capture promptly and follow leave/end rules; sign-out does not authorize background recording.

use_cases.title: Recover forgotten password
use_cases.preconditions: The recovery screens are enabled. The API implements them; the PA3 UI keeps them switched off until real email delivery is verified.
use_cases.trigger: Visitor selects Forgot password, or a signed-in learner selects Change password on Profile.
steps: Visitor submits an email address to the recovery form.
System returns a uniform acknowledgement and sends a single-use, expiring reset code if the account is eligible.
Visitor enters the email, the code and a new valid password on Reset password.
System verifies and consumes the reset credential atomically, changes the password, ends every existing session of the account and directs the visitor to sign in.
use_cases.success: A verified reset changes the password once; visitor signs in separately.
use_cases.minimum: No password change occurs without a verified, unused recovery credential.
use_cases.special: The backend enforces code expiry and single use and stores only code hashes. A successful reset ends every session of the account. An email-verification code is never accepted as a reset code.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, email is unknown or ineligible.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, email is unknown or ineligible.
alternatives.outcome: Show the same acknowledgement; do not disclose account existence.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, the code is expired, invalid or already used.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, the code is expired, invalid or already used.
alternatives.outcome: Do not change the password; offer a fresh recovery request.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, password is invalid or delivery/service fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, password is invalid or delivery/service fails.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the account unchanged; show a generic recovery error or retry path without displaying the reset credential.

use_cases.title: Review active sessions
use_cases.preconditions: User is authenticated; own-session inspection is enabled.
use_cases.trigger: User opens Active sessions.
steps: System authorizes the current account and retrieves only its sessions.
System displays nonsecret session metadata and marks the current browser.
User inspects activity and refreshes the list.
System reconciles expired sessions and shows the current authorized list.
use_cases.success: User sees a current or explicitly stale list of their sessions.
use_cases.minimum: Session credentials and other users sessions are never exposed.
use_cases.special: This FR requires viewing sessions, not unrequested device-control functionality. Never show raw access/refresh tokens, token hashes or full secret cookie values.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, no other active session exists.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, no other active session exists.
alternatives.outcome: Show an explicit current-session-only or empty state, not sample devices.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1, the session expires or another account is requested.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, the session expires or another account is requested.
alternatives.outcome: Require sign-in or deny access without returning another account session metadata.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, retrieval fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, retrieval fails.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the last list visibly stale and offer refresh; do not imply a device was revoked.

use_cases.title: Delete own account and data
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated as the account to delete; deletion workflow is enabled.
use_cases.trigger: Learner selects Delete account.
steps: System explains immediate loss of access and deletion of associated learning data within seven days.
Learner reviews the affected data and separately confirms deletion.
System verifies identity, atomically soft-deletes the account and invalidates access.
System schedules cascading erasure of transcripts, analysis, reports and optional chat, then shows a nonsecret confirmation.
use_cases.success: Account access is disabled immediately and associated hard deletion is due within seven days.
use_cases.minimum: Cancellation changes nothing; accepted deletion never silently restores access when a worker fails.
use_cases.special: Confirm erasure scope across derived artifacts and future chat. Do not promise instant physical deletion or preserve shareable report links after revocation.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, learner cancels.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, learner cancels.
alternatives.outcome: Close the confirmation; account and data remain unchanged.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, identity is stale or confirmation is missing.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, identity is stale or confirmation is missing.
alternatives.outcome: Reject deletion and require authorized confirmation; do not enqueue erasure.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, erasure processing is temporarily unavailable.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, erasure processing is temporarily unavailable.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the account disabled, retain a retryable deletion job and expose outstanding status to authorized administration.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, deletion was already accepted.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, deletion was already accepted.
alternatives.outcome: Return the existing deletion outcome rather than scheduling duplicate jobs.

use_cases.title: Suspend or reactivate account
use_cases.preconditions: Moderator/Admin is authenticated with account-moderation permission.
use_cases.trigger: Admin opens an account moderation record.
steps: System verifies role and loads the authorized moderation status.
Admin selects Suspend or Reactivate and enters a reason.
System validates the transition, applies the access restriction/restoration and records the actor and reason.
System refreshes the account status without exposing private learning content.
use_cases.success: An authorized moderation decision changes account access with an attributable record.
use_cases.minimum: Unauthorized or failed requests cannot change account access.
use_cases.special: Suspension is distinct from account deletion; reactivation does not undo a pending erasure or authorize transcript browsing.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, admin cancels or requests an already-applied status.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, admin cancels or requests an already-applied status.
alternatives.outcome: Leave status unchanged or return the existing result without duplicate action.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1, caller lacks permission.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, caller lacks permission.
alternatives.outcome: Deny the action without loading sensitive account details.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, the record changed or the write fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, the record changed or the write fails.
alternatives.outcome: Reload the current moderation status; do not show an unconfirmed suspension/reactivation.

use_cases.title: Browse and select topics
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated; curated topics or the explicitly documented seed-topic list are available.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Topics or chooses a topic while creating a room.
steps: System displays active curated topics with category and CEFR difficulty.
Learner enters search text and optionally changes category/difficulty filters.
System returns matching active topics and shows the selected filters.
Learner opens a motion, reviews its detail and selects it for the room-creation form.
use_cases.success: An active topic is selected; no room or audio is created merely by browsing.
use_cases.minimum: No unavailable topic is silently substituted and no unauthorized catalog mutation occurs.
use_cases.special: PA3 topic API/filter is extra scope; a static seed list must be labelled accurately. CEFR choices are A2/B1/B2/C1.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 3, there are no matches.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, there are no matches.
alternatives.outcome: Show an empty state and Clear filters; preserve the query without inventing topics.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 2, personalized recommendations are requested.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, personalized recommendations are requested.
alternatives.outcome: Run UC-02-03 only when enabled; normal browsing remains available.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 4, the topic was retired after loading.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, the topic was retired after loading.
alternatives.outcome: Reject selection for a new room, refresh the list and keep unrelated form choices.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, catalog retrieval fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, catalog retrieval fails.
alternatives.outcome: Show a retry state; use documented seed options only when that build explicitly supports them.

use_cases.title: Manage topic library
use_cases.preconditions: Admin is authenticated and authorized to curate topics.
use_cases.trigger: Admin selects Create, Edit or Retire topic.
steps: System loads the authorized topic editor with motion, category, difficulty and suggested-vocabulary fields.
Admin enters a new motion or edits an existing topic, or selects Retire.
System validates the fields and asks confirmation before retiring an active topic.
System saves the decision and updates availability for new rooms while preserving historical debate references.
use_cases.success: The validated topic change is saved and reflected in future catalog results.
use_cases.minimum: Failed edits do not corrupt historical rooms or partially modify public topics.
use_cases.special: Retirement is a state change, not a destructive delete of motions referenced by finished debates.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 3, retirement is cancelled.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, retirement is cancelled.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the topic active and return to the editor.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, required fields or CEFR tags are invalid.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, required fields or CEFR tags are invalid.
alternatives.outcome: Show inline errors and preserve the last committed topic.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, another edit won or saving fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, another edit won or saving fails.
alternatives.outcome: Reload the current version and retain the admin draft for reconciliation.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 1, role is insufficient.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, role is insufficient.
alternatives.outcome: Deny access; do not expose editing controls as authorization.

use_cases.title: Get personalized topic recommendations
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated; recommendations are enabled and the curated catalog is available.
use_cases.trigger: At topic discovery, learner requests Recommended topics.
steps: System reads the learner self-assessed CEFR and available, authorized practice observations.
System ranks active topics using those inputs and explains the matching reason.
Learner reviews or dismisses a recommendation.
A selected topic returns to ordinary room creation; learner may instead browse without personalization.
use_cases.success: Learner receives transparent optional topic suggestions or an honest fallback.
use_cases.minimum: No recommendation changes the learner CEFR or forces topic selection.
use_cases.special: This extends UC-02-01; it does not block browsing, certify ability, or infer weaknesses from another learner data.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, no history exists.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, no history exists.
alternatives.outcome: Use the self-assessed level only and disclose the limited basis.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 2, no suitable topic is active.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, no suitable topic is active.
alternatives.outcome: Show no recommendations and offer the complete curated catalog.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, ranking is unavailable.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, ranking is unavailable.
alternatives.outcome: Keep browsing usable and avoid a fabricated personal rationale.

use_cases.title: Propose a custom topic
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated; custom-topic moderation is enabled.
use_cases.trigger: Learner chooses Propose topic.
steps: Learner enters a proposed motion, category and suggested difficulty.
System validates the submission and records it as pending moderation.
Admin reviews the pending proposal using authorized moderation controls.
System publishes only an approved curated topic, or records a rejection and shows the proposer its status.
use_cases.success: The proposal has an attributable pending, approved or rejected moderation outcome.
use_cases.minimum: A learner submission is never automatically a public topic.
use_cases.special: Stretch design only. The public-topic editor and this submission queue have different permissions.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, learner cancels.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, learner cancels.
alternatives.outcome: Discard the unsent draft without creating a public topic.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, content is empty, invalid or rate limited.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, content is empty, invalid or rate limited.
alternatives.outcome: Show the reason and preserve safe draft text; no queue item is created.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, admin rejects or requests revision.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, admin rejects or requests revision.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the proposal nonpublic and show the moderation outcome to its proposer.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, publication fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, publication fails.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the proposal pending/retryable; do not list it publicly as approved.

use_cases.title: Create debate room
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated and has selected an active topic.
use_cases.trigger: Learner selects Create room.
steps: System shows topic, stance mode, format and duration with supported defaults.
Learner reviews options and submits; creator stance is provided only for CREATOR_PICKS.
System validates the topic/options and atomically creates the LOBBY and creator membership A.
System displays the invite code/link, lobby expiry and waiting status; no microphone, media or STT starts.
use_cases.success: One LOBBY and creator seat A exist with an expiring invite.
use_cases.minimum: A failed transaction leaves no orphan room or membership.
use_cases.special: Exactly two debater seats; duration integer 60–1800 seconds; lobby 30 minutes; eight-character secure invite. Build 1 uses /rooms, not an arbitrary status endpoint.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, optional settings are unchanged.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, optional settings are unchanged.
alternatives.outcome: Use FREE_FLOW, 600 seconds and RANDOM.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, topic is unavailable or duration/stance/format is invalid.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, topic is unavailable or duration/stance/format is invalid.
alternatives.outcome: Return field errors and create neither room nor membership.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, generated invite code collides.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, generated invite code collides.
alternatives.outcome: Generate another secure code within a bounded server retry; never expose a duplicate code.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 4, response is lost or creation fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, response is lost or creation fails.
alternatives.outcome: Reconcile the created resource before repeating creation; do not announce a room that was not confirmed.

use_cases.title: Join invited room
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated and has an invite code or link.
use_cases.trigger: Learner submits Join room.
steps: Learner opens an invite link or enters the eight-character code.
System normalizes the code, resolves and locks the room, and checks expiry and joinable state.
System returns an existing member snapshot on retry; otherwise reserves the free second seat for this identity.
System assigns opposing stances and transitions LOBBY to READY atomically.
System displays the authoritative lobby to both learners without treating membership as consent.
use_cases.success: Caller occupies exactly one seat; the two-member room is READY with opposing stances.
use_cases.minimum: Capacity never exceeds two, including concurrent requests.
use_cases.special: Server identity comes from auth; lock plus unique seat/membership constraints enforce capacity. No consent value is inferred or copied from the partner.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 3, caller is already a participant.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, caller is already a participant.
alternatives.outcome: Return their authorized snapshot; do not insert another seat or perform a READY self-transition.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, invite is unknown/expired or malformed.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, invite is unknown/expired or malformed.
alternatives.outcome: Show unavailable/validation feedback without room contents; allow editing the invite.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, room already has two distinct learners, including a concurrent join winner.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, room already has two distinct learners, including a concurrent join winner.
alternatives.outcome: Reject the third with ROOM_FULL; do not reveal participant details.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 2, room is LIVE, ENDED or CANCELLED.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, room is LIVE, ENDED or CANCELLED.
alternatives.outcome: Return ROOM_NOT_JOINABLE; keep membership unchanged.

alternatives.label: E4 — At step 4, transaction/network fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, transaction/network fails.
alternatives.outcome: Rollback or reload the authorized snapshot before retry; no duplicate participant or stance assignment.

use_cases.title: View lobby and readiness
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is a current authenticated room participant.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens or refreshes their lobby.
steps: System checks membership and loads the room, applying expiry before returning state.
System shows topic, format, duration, invite access, seat occupancy and stances.
System updates authoritative state using the build supported transport; Build 1 polls every two seconds.
Learner sees LOBBY, READY or terminal state and the separate consent/microphone gates when those features are supported.
use_cases.success: Learner sees current authorized room state with distinct presence and processing gates.
use_cases.minimum: No private snapshot leaks and a stale view does not authorize live capture.
use_cases.special: A Build 1 Start control is disabled with a clear unavailable explanation; do not create media or future endpoints to animate the prototype.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 3, second learner joins or leaves.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, second learner joins or leaves.
alternatives.outcome: Refresh presence and state; READY reflects occupied seats, not recording permission.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 1, a LOBBY/READY room expired.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, a LOBBY/READY room expired.
alternatives.outcome: Apply CANCELLED and display expiry to members; the invite cannot admit anyone.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1, caller is not a member or room is absent.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, caller is not a member or room is absent.
alternatives.outcome: Return a non-disclosing unavailable view with no participants/invite.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, updates fail or arrive stale.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, updates fail or arrive stale.
alternatives.outcome: Mark the view stale and retry; do not enable start from stale readiness.

alternatives.label: A3 — At step 3, learner leaves the page, signs out or reaches a terminal state.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, learner leaves the page, signs out or reaches a terminal state.
alternatives.outcome: Stop polling/subscriptions and any local test capture.

use_cases.title: Give or withdraw processing consent
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated, belongs to the room and processing consent controls are implemented.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens the processing notice or changes their own consent.
steps: System explains transcript capture, AI processing, retention/deletion and how to decline or withdraw.
Learner independently selects Agree or Decline; controls are unchecked by default.
System records only this learner decision and current notice version/timestamp.
System updates readiness; withdrawal during LIVE immediately stops capture and ends the session safely.
use_cases.success: The learner own informed decision is recorded and enforced by the server.
use_cases.minimum: Unconfirmed, declined or withdrawn consent cannot authorize further audio/STT transmission.
use_cases.special: Room presence, account terms, browser permission and another learner decision are not substitutes for consent. New audience/chat processing grants remain separate.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, learner declines.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, learner declines.
alternatives.outcome: Keep LIVE unavailable without account penalty; allow leaving or ordinary account use.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, partner has not consented or the notice changed.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, partner has not consented or the notice changed.
alternatives.outcome: Keep start disabled and request a fresh personal decision where necessary.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, save fails or identity/membership is stale.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, save fails or identity/membership is stale.
alternatives.outcome: Show consent unconfirmed, keep start blocked and require retry or sign-in.

alternatives.label: A3 — At step 4, learner withdraws while LIVE or loses network during withdrawal.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, learner withdraws while LIVE or loses network during withdrawal.
alternatives.outcome: Stop local transmission immediately, request authoritative end, and reconcile server state before any resume.

use_cases.title: Start debate
use_cases.preconditions: Two authenticated participants occupy READY; session start/media implementation is available.
use_cases.trigger: A participant selects Start debate.
steps: System invokes UC-03-13 to revalidate room state, both members, expiry, current dual consent, mic results and media capability.
System authorizes the start and atomically records LIVE and the authoritative timer origin.
System issues scoped media authorization and establishes independent tracks only after the gate succeeds.
System shows LIVE, timer, mute/end controls and visible transmission/transcription indicators to both participants.
use_cases.success: A single authorized LIVE session exists with consent-gated media and synchronized timer origin.
use_cases.minimum: No failed start bypasses consent or leaves background transmission active.
use_cases.special: This future-media contract is not enabled by the SCRUM-28 pure transition function. Start requires actual media capability, not a hardcoded ready flag.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1, consent/mic/presence/expiry is missing or stale.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, consent/mic/presence/expiry is missing or stale.
alternatives.outcome: Reject start with a specific safe gate explanation; publish no audio.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 1, only the Build 1 lobby slice exists or media is unavailable.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, only the Build 1 lobby slice exists or media is unavailable.
alternatives.outcome: Keep Start disabled/deny the operation; no simulated LIVE or hidden recording.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, simultaneous starts race.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, simultaneous starts race.
alternatives.outcome: Accept only one READY→LIVE transition and reconcile the existing authorized LIVE snapshot.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 3, media setup fails or consent is withdrawn.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, media setup fails or consent is withdrawn.
alternatives.outcome: Stop capture and perform safe session recovery/end; never leave a screen claiming healthy LIVE audio.

use_cases.title: Leave or end debate
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is an authenticated participant in a nonterminal room.
use_cases.trigger: Learner selects Leave before LIVE or End debate while LIVE.
steps: System keeps the leave/end action accessible and stops this browser transmission promptly when leaving.
System validates the caller membership and current authoritative state.
Before LIVE, system removes the departing seat and clears relevant readiness/consent; READY returns to LOBBY, or authorized cancellation terminates the lobby.
During LIVE, system transitions to ENDED, stops all capture/STT, records end time and notifies the partner.
System offers the ended-session view and queues eligible post-debate analysis without delaying the exit.
use_cases.success: Departure or ending is persisted and transmission ceases; any eligible analysis has explicit status.
use_cases.minimum: Exit never depends on AI availability and a terminal state never becomes LIVE again.
use_cases.special: Both participants may end LIVE; a prompt must not trap someone in an unsafe debate. Creator cancellation uses CANCELLED only before LIVE.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, room is already ENDED/CANCELLED.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, room is already ENDED/CANCELLED.
alternatives.outcome: Return the terminal outcome; do not reopen or enqueue duplicate analysis.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, the server cannot be reached.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, the server cannot be reached.
alternatives.outcome: Stop local capture, show end confirmation pending and reconcile/retry the server request.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 5, fewer than 60 seconds of speech exist.
alternatives.detail: At step 5, fewer than 60 seconds of speech exist.
alternatives.outcome: Show insufficient speech for assessment and do not invent scores.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 5, analysis enqueue fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 5, analysis enqueue fails.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the room ended and capture stopped; show retryable analysis status separately.

use_cases.title: Follow debate and turn timers
use_cases.preconditions: Learner belongs to a LIVE session and timing transport is implemented.
use_cases.trigger: Session begins or learner opens the LIVE view.
steps: System loads authoritative start time, duration and debate format.
System displays the overall countdown; timed-turn mode also displays the active stage/speaker and turn countdown.
System reconciles updates with server time while preserving audibility and visible end controls.
At overall expiry, server ends the session and clients show ENDED rather than a locally extended timer.
use_cases.success: Displayed timing follows the session authority and final expiry ends the session once.
use_cases.minimum: Client clock manipulation does not change room duration or consent.
use_cases.special: Timed turns are guidance, not automatic audio enforcement. Browser suspension/reconnect must fetch the current stage rather than replaying old ticks.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, format is FREE_FLOW.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, format is FREE_FLOW.
alternatives.outcome: Show only the overall debate timer, without invented turn restrictions.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, timer events are lost or browser clock differs.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, timer events are lost or browser clock differs.
alternatives.outcome: Mark timing stale and resynchronize from server state; do not restart or extend the debate.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 4, participant ends before expiry.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, participant ends before expiry.
alternatives.outcome: Stop the display at the authoritative ended state.

alternatives.label: A3 — At step 2, a timed turn expires.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, a timed turn expires.
alternatives.outcome: Advance the visible stage/turn marker; do not hard-mute the other participant.

use_cases.title: Report abusive behavior
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is an authenticated participant with access to the room or transcript being reported.
use_cases.trigger: Learner selects Report abuse.
steps: System opens a report form while preserving a readily accessible leave/end action.
Learner selects a reason, optionally references an authorized transcript segment and enters factual context.
System validates membership and stores the report for the moderation queue.
System confirms receipt privately without promising a verdict or forcing continued participation.
use_cases.success: An authorized report is queued with an honest receipt.
use_cases.minimum: Reporting failure never blocks exit or publicly labels a participant guilty.
use_cases.special: Report details are not posted to the opponent or fed to a public leaderboard. Moderator access is limited to the evidence needed for the case.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, learner cancels or chooses Leave/End.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, learner cancels or chooses Leave/End.
alternatives.outcome: Discard the unsent report and permit immediate exit.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, reason/reference is invalid or outside room access.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, reason/reference is invalid or outside room access.
alternatives.outcome: Reject the report with safe field feedback; expose no other transcript.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, reporting is unavailable or rate limited.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, reporting is unavailable or rate limited.
alternatives.outcome: Show pending/not sent with a retry option; leaving remains available.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, a retry duplicates the same submission.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, a retry duplicates the same submission.
alternatives.outcome: Return the existing report receipt instead of spamming the queue.

use_cases.title: Review abuse and close room
use_cases.preconditions: Admin has report-review and room-closure permission.
use_cases.trigger: Admin opens a pending abuse report.
steps: System loads the report and the minimum authorized supporting context.
Admin reviews it, chooses an outcome and records a reason.
For closure, system rechecks the current room and applies CANCELLED before LIVE or ENDED during LIVE.
System stops active transmission when needed, notifies participants neutrally and records the moderation outcome.
use_cases.success: An attributable moderation outcome and any authorized closure are persisted.
use_cases.minimum: No unauthorized closure or private-content disclosure occurs.
use_cases.special: Do not add LIVE→CANCELLED to simplify closure. A moderation permission is not blanket permission to browse every learner transcript.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, report is dismissed or needs further review.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, report is dismissed or needs further review.
alternatives.outcome: Record that outcome without changing room state or making a guilt claim.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, room already ended/was cancelled.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, room already ended/was cancelled.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the terminal state and record review without duplicate end jobs.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1, caller lacks permission.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, caller lacks permission.
alternatives.outcome: Deny access without disclosing evidence or participant details.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, closure fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, closure fails.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the moderation outcome pending and retry from current room state; do not announce confirmed closure.

use_cases.title: Use private room text chat
use_cases.preconditions: Post-MVP feature is separately approved and enabled; two authenticated debaters occupy the room.
use_cases.trigger: Creator enables room chat and a participant opens it.
steps: System checks creator authority and enables the private two-debater text channel.
Participant composes and submits a message.
System validates room membership and stores the message separately from the speech transcript.
System delivers it to the other debater; chat stays excluded from AI processing unless both separately opted in.
use_cases.success: An authorized private message is stored separately and delivered with processing restrictions.
use_cases.minimum: Chat never silently becomes transcript or AI input.
use_cases.special: Design only; no class/group chat, audience publishing, public messaging or moderation bot is added by this use case.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, creator has not enabled chat.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, creator has not enabled chat.
alternatives.outcome: Show chat unavailable and accept no messages.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, caller is an audience member/nonparticipant or the message is invalid.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, caller is an audience member/nonparticipant or the message is invalid.
alternatives.outcome: Reject submission without exposing chat history.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, delivery confirmation is lost.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, delivery confirmation is lost.
alternatives.outcome: Show pending and reconcile the message identity before retry, avoiding duplicates.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 4, either debater declines chat analysis or account data is deleted.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, either debater declines chat analysis or account data is deleted.
alternatives.outcome: Exclude chat from analysis and include its stored records in the applicable deletion cascade.

use_cases.title: Practise solo with an AI opponent
use_cases.preconditions: Post-MVP solo-practice feature, a reviewed solo consent model and a TTS adapter contract exist; learner is authenticated.
use_cases.trigger: Learner chooses Solo practice.
steps: System labels the opponent as AI and explains text generation, speech synthesis and personal audio processing.
Learner explicitly grants their own processing consent and initiates a local mic test.
System creates the separately specified solo session and obtains a bounded generated opponent turn through LLMAdapter.
System speaks the AI turn through the future TTS adapter and exchanges turns with the consenting learner.
Learner ends practice; system stops capture and shows the permitted session outcome.
use_cases.success: A separately authorized solo session finishes with the AI identity and processing basis explicit.
use_cases.minimum: No other human audio is used and an AI never counts as a consenting human.
use_cases.special: This design intentionally does not weaken the current FR-11 two-debater invariant. Solo states, TTS and token/cost controls require future architectural approval.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1, solo/TTS/consent prerequisites are not implemented.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, solo/TTS/consent prerequisites are not implemented.
alternatives.outcome: Show unavailable; do not repurpose a two-human room or fake a consenting second person.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, learner declines or withdraws consent.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, learner declines or withdraws consent.
alternatives.outcome: Start no capture, or stop immediately and end an active solo session.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3 or 4, LLM/TTS fails or exceeds budget.
alternatives.detail: At step 3 or 4, LLM/TTS fails or exceeds budget.
alternatives.outcome: Stop generated audio, disclose the unavailable turn and allow a safe retry/end without fabricated responses.

use_cases.title: Authorize and join audience access
use_cases.preconditions: Post-MVP audience feature is enabled; creator and both debaters have current room access.
use_cases.trigger: Creator requests audience access and an invited audience member attempts to join.
steps: Creator sets a bounded audience allowance and explains which media/transcript would be shared.
Each debater independently grants or declines audience sharing.
System verifies both grants and audience identity/capacity before issuing subscribe-only access.
Audience member views only authorized media/transcript while the system enforces no publishing and no grading rights.
System revokes audience subscriptions when consent is withdrawn or the room ends.
use_cases.success: Authorized audience can receive only permitted content under current dual sharing consent.
use_cases.minimum: Audience never occupies either debater seat, publishes audio or receives unconsented content.
use_cases.special: Audience capacity values and revocation latency need the future media contract; no unlimited audience or account-role bypass is assumed.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, either debater declines or has not answered.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, either debater declines or has not answered.
alternatives.outcome: Keep audience outside the room and expose no audio or transcript.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, audience cap is reached or invite/identity is invalid.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, audience cap is reached or invite/identity is invalid.
alternatives.outcome: Deny entry without leaking room content.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, audience attempts to publish or grade.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, audience attempts to publish or grade.
alternatives.outcome: Reject the operation; audience status does not grant evaluator or debater rights.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 5, either debater revokes sharing.
alternatives.detail: At step 5, either debater revokes sharing.
alternatives.outcome: Revoke access promptly; a reconnect must revalidate current grants.

use_cases.title: Validate start readiness
use_cases.preconditions: An authenticated participant start request invokes this supporting subcase; server can read current room authority.
use_cases.trigger: UC-03-05 requests mandatory start validation.
steps: System reads the current locked/versioned room and authenticated participant membership.
System verifies READY, two distinct seats and a lobby deadline strictly after server time.
System checks current consent and local mic-readiness results separately for both learners.
System verifies actual media capability and returns a permit for the same atomic start decision.
use_cases.success: A start permit is valid only for the checked current transaction/context.
use_cases.minimum: Every failed or unavailable gate fails closed without audio transmission.
use_cases.special: Supporting behavior, not a public Validate endpoint. The readiness inspector prototype represents learner-visible gate status, not server-debug internals.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1 or 2, caller is not a participant, state is stale, capacity differs or deadline expired.
alternatives.detail: At step 1 or 2, caller is not a participant, state is stale, capacity differs or deadline expired.
alternatives.outcome: Return a non-disclosing denial or expiry outcome; no start permit.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, either consent or mic result is missing, revoked or stale.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, either consent or mic result is missing, revoked or stale.
alternatives.outcome: Return the missing gate and keep publication disabled.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 4, media is unsupported/unavailable or state changed after checking.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, media is unsupported/unavailable or state changed after checking.
alternatives.outcome: Reject and revalidate current authority before any retry; no reusable stale permit.

use_cases.title: Select and test microphone
use_cases.preconditions: Learner has opened pre-debate setup in a browser with a supported microphone API.
use_cases.trigger: Learner explicitly selects Test microphone.
steps: System explains that this is a local-only test and requests browser microphone permission after the click.
Learner selects an available input device and speaks a short sample.
System shows a local level meter and test result without uploading, storing, transcribing or publishing audio.
Learner confirms the result or selects another device; system releases the local test track when the test ends.
use_cases.success: A usable selected input has a current local test result and no pre-consent network audio.
use_cases.minimum: A failed/cancelled test cannot satisfy microphone readiness or initiate remote transmission.
use_cases.special: Browser permission is distinct from processing consent. READY still represents presence; mic denial blocks LIVE rather than changing the occupied-seat definition.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1, microphone permission is denied.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, microphone permission is denied.
alternatives.outcome: Show browser recovery instructions and Keep mic test incomplete; no repeated permission loop or silent capture.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 2, no device exists, device is busy/unplugged or no signal is detected.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, no device exists, device is busy/unplugged or no signal is detected.
alternatives.outcome: Show device-specific recovery, allow another input and leave mic readiness false.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 3, learner cancels or leaves setup.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, learner cancels or leaves setup.
alternatives.outcome: Stop/release the local test track immediately without recording a passed test.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 4, learner changes input after passing.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, learner changes input after passing.
alternatives.outcome: Invalidate the old result and test the newly selected device before start.

use_cases.title: Exchange audio and control mute
use_cases.preconditions: Room is authoritatively LIVE; both debaters have current consent and usable selected inputs.
use_cases.trigger: Authorized LIVE media connects and a participant speaks or selects Mute.
steps: System obtains scoped media access and connects the two debaters using separate LiveKit audio tracks.
System displays both participants mic/speaking status and visible transmission/processing indicators.
Learner mutes or unmutes their own microphone; system changes only their publishing state and confirms the actual state.
System maintains audibility and accessible end/leave controls while optional analysis runs independently.
When the room ends or consent is withdrawn, system stops publication, subscriptions and capture.
use_cases.success: Consented independent tracks carry live speech; own mute and terminal stopping behavior are observable.
use_cases.minimum: No participant controls the opponent microphone or continues publication after ending/withdrawal.
use_cases.special: Prioritize audio latency over analysis. Raw audio is not persisted by default; independent tracks preserve deterministic speaker attribution.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 3, learner mutes.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, learner mutes.
alternatives.outcome: Stop publishing own speech while preserving the partner audio; show Muted rather than Disconnected.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1 or 3, media authorization fails or consent/state is no longer valid.
alternatives.detail: At step 1 or 3, media authorization fails or consent/state is no longer valid.
alternatives.outcome: Publish no further audio; reconcile room authority and show recovery/end controls.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, STT/AI fails while audio remains healthy.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, STT/AI fails while audio remains healthy.
alternatives.outcome: Continue consented audio and disclose the unavailable processing section without blocking conversation.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 4, optional video or overlays are requested.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, optional video or overlays are requested.
alternatives.outcome: Invoke only the enabled, separately authorized UC-04-04/UC-08-02 extensions.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 4, media connection drops.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, media connection drops.
alternatives.outcome: Show recovery status and invoke UC-04-03; never display a successful unmute when no track is publishing.

use_cases.title: Recover a dropped connection
use_cases.preconditions: Learner was a member of a LIVE room and their connection becomes interrupted.
use_cases.trigger: System detects loss of the participant media/event connection.
steps: System shows a connection-quality/reconnecting banner and starts the authoritative 60-second grace window.
Client attempts bounded reconnection using the same authenticated participant identity.
Server rechecks membership, consent, room state and current grace deadline before restoring media.
System loads the current timer/state and resumes missed transcript events without duplicate segments.
use_cases.success: The same authorized participant resumes within grace or the room ends safely.
use_cases.minimum: Reconnection cannot bypass consent, duplicate a seat, restart the timer or reopen a terminal room.
use_cases.special: Default grace is 60 seconds. Early-end analysis requires at least 60 seconds of speech; show insufficient evidence otherwise.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 3, reconnect succeeds before grace expiry.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, reconnect succeeds before grace expiry.
alternatives.outcome: Restore the existing seat/tracks and actual current timer; do not create a new room or consent record.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, grace expires or room already ended.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, grace expires or room already ended.
alternatives.outcome: Transition/retain ENDED, stop capture and show the ended-session view.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, identity or consent no longer authorizes media.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, identity or consent no longer authorizes media.
alternatives.outcome: Deny publication and require sign-in/consent recovery only where the current room lifecycle permits.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 2, connectivity remains unavailable.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, connectivity remains unavailable.
alternatives.outcome: Keep retry timing visible and allow safe local exit; never extend the server grace from the client.

use_cases.title: Enable optional live video
use_cases.preconditions: Optional video is explicitly enabled and separately specified; consented audio already works.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opts into video at media setup or during LIVE.
steps: System explains optional video sharing and requests a separate personal opt-in.
Learner explicitly grants camera permission and selects a device.
System verifies current audience/participant sharing permissions and publishes the authorized video track.
Learner can turn video off independently; system keeps audio controls and audio priority intact.
use_cases.success: Only separately authorized optional video is visible and independently stoppable.
use_cases.minimum: Video failure/decline never prevents the core audio workflow or activates hidden camera capture.
use_cases.special: Stretch design; no video recording is implied. This is an extension of UC-04-02 and does not expand existing audience permissions.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, learner declines or optional video is disabled.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, learner declines or optional video is disabled.
alternatives.outcome: Continue the audio-only debate with no penalty or camera request.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, camera permission/device fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, camera permission/device fails.
alternatives.outcome: Show recovery and remain audio-only; never infer permission from mic access.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, bandwidth degrades or sharing consent is revoked.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, bandwidth degrades or sharing consent is revoked.
alternatives.outcome: Stop video first and disclose its state while preserving authorized audio where possible.

use_cases.title: View speaker-attributed live transcript
use_cases.preconditions: Learner belongs to a consented LIVE room; authorized STT and transcript transport are available.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens the live transcript while speech occurs.
steps: System checks room membership and processing consent, then subscribes the worker to independent participant tracks.
STT returns timestamped partial text; system displays it with the deterministic track-linked speaker and provisional status.
When a final result arrives, system validates timing/confidence, persists the segment idempotently and replaces the partial text.
System updates both debaters views and lets the learner inspect low-confidence words or flag a mis-transcribed segment.
use_cases.success: Authorized readers see speaker-linked partial/final text with honest confidence and no duplicate final segments.
use_cases.minimum: No unconsented transcription or guessed speaker identity is used as confirmed learner evidence.
use_cases.special: Partial hypotheses are not persisted. Final segments include word timing/confidence where required; preserve fillers rather than cleaning away learning signals.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, both learners speak simultaneously.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, both learners speak simultaneously.
alternatives.outcome: Display two attributable streams with overlap metadata rather than merging speaker identities.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, a final/event is duplicated or replays after reconnect.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, a final/event is duplicated or replays after reconnect.
alternatives.outcome: Upsert by session/speaker/sequence and de-duplicate client events; show one final segment.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2 or 3, STT fails or timing/confidence is missing.
alternatives.detail: At step 2 or 3, STT fails or timing/confidence is missing.
alternatives.outcome: Mark transcription unavailable/uncertain; keep healthy audio running and do not invent text or metrics.

alternatives.label: A3 — At step 4, learner flags recognition error or confidence is low.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, learner flags recognition error or confidence is low.
alternatives.outcome: Mark the affected span for exclusion from confirmed language criticism; preserve the original attributable evidence.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 1, consent or membership is revoked.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, consent or membership is revoked.
alternatives.outcome: Stop the subscription/capture path and deny further transcript delivery.

use_cases.title: Review and export full transcript
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated and is a participant in the ended debate.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Transcript or selects Export text/Markdown.
steps: System verifies participant access and loads finalized segments in stable time/speaker order.
System shows speaker labels, timestamps, recognition caveats and any flagged spans.
Learner selects text or Markdown export and reviews its content scope.
System generates the authorized export and starts a local download.
use_cases.success: Learner can review and optionally download only the authorized transcript version.
use_cases.minimum: An export failure changes neither transcript nor access permissions.
use_cases.special: No raw audio download is implied. Exported filenames and Markdown text must be safe and must not include session credentials.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, no speech or only partial transcript exists.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, no speech or only partial transcript exists.
alternatives.outcome: Show an empty/partial view and label any export accordingly; do not manufacture missing turns.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1 or 4, membership/data availability changed or debate was deleted.
alternatives.detail: At step 1 or 4, membership/data availability changed or debate was deleted.
alternatives.outcome: Deny access without returning transcript bytes or another participant metadata.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, generation/download fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, generation/download fails.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the review view usable and offer retry; do not claim a file was downloaded.

use_cases.title: Use mixed-audio diarization fallback
use_cases.preconditions: Stretch mixed-audio path is enabled and separately authorized; participants have explicitly consented.
use_cases.trigger: Learner is offered the supported mixed-audio fallback after the primary track path cannot be used.
steps: System explains that mixed-audio diarization has lower speaker-attribution certainty and is outside MVP scoring.
Learner explicitly accepts the fallback; system validates membership and current processing consent.
System sends only the authorized mixed stream through the configured fallback/diarization service.
System displays timestamped fallback text and uncertain speaker labels without treating them as deterministic track identity.
use_cases.success: An explicitly authorized fallback produces transparently limited transcript text.
use_cases.minimum: The primary deterministic attribution contract is never silently replaced by statistical labels.
use_cases.special: The proposed mixed-audio WebSocket is future-only; this use case adds no working upload endpoint to PA3.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, learner declines or fallback is disabled.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, learner declines or fallback is disabled.
alternatives.outcome: Send no mixed audio; allow a safe primary-path retry or ending the session.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, provider is unavailable or consent is withdrawn.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, provider is unavailable or consent is withdrawn.
alternatives.outcome: Stop fallback transmission and show unavailable status without recording by default.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, diarization cannot confidently identify the speaker.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, diarization cannot confidently identify the speaker.
alternatives.outcome: Show unknown/uncertain speaker and exclude the span from speaker-specific MVP scoring.

use_cases.title: Review language corrections
use_cases.preconditions: Learner has authorized access to an ended debate with usable own finalized transcript and CEFR context.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Language feedback.
steps: System loads eligible own-speaker segments and excludes flagged/low-confidence evidence from confirmed error claims.
Language Coach returns schema-validated grammar/vocabulary items with exact quote, correction and explanation.
System invokes UC-06-05 for every retained item and ranks valid findings by learning impact/frequency.
System displays a CEFR-appropriate number of priority items and links each to its original transcript context.
use_cases.success: Displayed corrections are attributable, CEFR-appropriate and paired with concrete remediation.
use_cases.minimum: Unavailable analysis never becomes a fabricated correction or a zero score.
use_cases.special: Default priority-item caps: A2 3, B1 5, B2 7, C1 10. Do not interrupt LIVE speech with dense feedback; a matched quote alone does not prove a grammar error.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, usable speech is insufficient or no grounded issue is found.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, usable speech is insufficient or no grounded issue is found.
alternatives.outcome: Explain limited evidence/no retained findings; do not invent errors or issue false praise.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, provider times out or returns invalid schema.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, provider times out or returns invalid schema.
alternatives.outcome: Retry the schema repair once as specified; then mark the language section unavailable.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, quote/speaker/segment validation fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, quote/speaker/segment validation fails.
alternatives.outcome: Discard the item with an internal reason; never display fabricated learner wording.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 4, learner inspects an uncertain or flagged transcription.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, learner inspects an uncertain or flagged transcription.
alternatives.outcome: Show the recognition caveat and evidence flag workflow rather than treating the criticism as confirmed.

use_cases.title: Review speaking metrics
use_cases.preconditions: Learner can access own finalized transcript with sufficient validated word timing.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Speaking metrics.
steps: System selects eligible speaker segments and validates word/speech-time inputs.
Deterministic code computes WPM, filler rate, pause profile, talk-time share, MATTR lexical diversity and mean sentence length.
System displays the measured values with units, sample size and short definitions.
Learner opens a metric explanation and the supporting transcript range.
use_cases.success: Learner sees reproducible own-speaker measurements or explicitly unavailable values.
use_cases.minimum: No LLM estimates replace missing deterministic measurements.
use_cases.special: WPM excludes silences over 2 seconds; pauses use at least 0.8 seconds; MATTR uses window 50. Filler handling needs context for words such as like/so; metrics are formative, not proficiency certification.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, there is no speech or a denominator/window has insufficient data.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, there is no speech or a denominator/window has insufficient data.
alternatives.outcome: Display Not enough data for affected metrics; do not divide by zero or fabricate zero-performance scores.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, word timestamps are absent, unordered or invalid.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, word timestamps are absent, unordered or invalid.
alternatives.outcome: Mark timing-dependent metrics unavailable and expose the measurement limitation.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, overlapping speech occurs.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, overlapping speech occurs.
alternatives.outcome: Compute each participant from their own track/timestamps and explain overlap rather than merging counts.

use_cases.title: Review recurring language patterns
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated; recurring-pattern analysis is enabled and grounded feedback exists.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Recurring language patterns.
steps: System loads only authorized retained findings from the selected debate/date range.
System groups comparable categories and counts distinct grounded examples.
System shows recurring patterns with source debate links, example quotes and a suggested practice focus.
Learner opens an example to inspect context or changes the comparison range.
use_cases.success: Pattern summaries are backed by accessible, comparable own-speaker evidence.
use_cases.minimum: No other learner history is exposed or used to infer personal weaknesses.
use_cases.special: Avoid diagnosing a stable personal defect from one sentence. Counts are observations of retained evidence, not certified error rates.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, too few eligible findings exist.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, too few eligible findings exist.
alternatives.outcome: Show insufficient history and the available examples without inventing recurrence.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 2, rubric/prompt versions or transcript eligibility differ.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, rubric/prompt versions or transcript eligibility differ.
alternatives.outcome: Separate incompatible groups and disclose comparison limits.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 4, source evidence was deleted or flagged.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, source evidence was deleted or flagged.
alternatives.outcome: Remove/recompute the affected example/count and show unavailable evidence rather than a broken authoritative claim.

use_cases.title: Review pronunciation assessment
use_cases.preconditions: Stretch assessment provider and an explicit audio-processing consent contract are available.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opts into Pronunciation assessment.
steps: System explains the external provider, needed audio and indicative assessment limits.
Learner explicitly permits the assessment and initiates any required sample capture.
System sends only the authorized sample through the assessment adapter.
System shows provider-qualified word-level feedback and a concrete practice suggestion, then stops sample capture.
use_cases.success: Learner receives separately authorized, clearly limited pronunciation feedback.
use_cases.minimum: No undisclosed sample upload, raw-audio retention or accent-based reasoning judgment occurs.
use_cases.special: STT confidence is not pronunciation accuracy. Provider selection, sample retention and limits require a future reviewed contract; no working provider is claimed here.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, learner declines or cancels.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, learner declines or cancels.
alternatives.outcome: Send no sample and keep ordinary transcript/language feedback usable.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, audio is unusable or provider fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, audio is unusable or provider fails.
alternatives.outcome: Show insufficient audio/unavailable status, stop capture and allow a deliberate retry.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, provider result is unsupported/invalid.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, provider result is unsupported/invalid.
alternatives.outcome: Withhold the assessment rather than converting STT confidence into a pronunciation score.

use_cases.title: Validate cited transcript evidence
use_cases.preconditions: A feedback consumer supplies authorized transcript segments and a candidate item with speaker, segment and quote.
use_cases.trigger: Language/Argument feedback invokes mandatory evidence validation.
steps: System validates the candidate schema and requires a nonblank quote and speaker/segment reference.
System resolves exactly the referenced segment within the authorized transcript and verifies its speaker.
System checks that the quote is an exact contiguous substring of that segment without fuzzy correction or cross-segment concatenation.
System returns accepted evidence or a structured rejection so the parent workflow keeps only valid items.
use_cases.success: Accepted evidence has a nonempty verbatim quote in the correct authorized speaker segment.
use_cases.minimum: Invalid evidence never reaches learner-facing feedback as a valid citation.
use_cases.special: Supporting behavior; the learner-facing prototype is a citation/context inspector, not a private model-debug endpoint. Grounding is provenance validation and does not establish critique correctness.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1, the quote is empty/whitespace or references are missing.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, the quote is empty/whitespace or references are missing.
alternatives.outcome: Reject the candidate; require a new attributable item rather than guessing evidence.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 2, the segment is absent, unauthorized, or belongs to another speaker.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, the segment is absent, unauthorized, or belongs to another speaker.
alternatives.outcome: Reject without leaking the other transcript or remapping speaker identity.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 3, quote is paraphrased, normalized, reordered or stitched across segments.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, quote is paraphrased, normalized, reordered or stitched across segments.
alternatives.outcome: Reject the nonverbatim quote; do not silently rewrite it to pass.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 4, exact words match but recognition is low-confidence/flagged.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, exact words match but recognition is low-confidence/flagged.
alternatives.outcome: Provenance may match, but the parent eligibility policy withholds confirmed learner-error claims.

use_cases.title: Review argument structure and rebuttals
use_cases.preconditions: Learner may access an ended debate with sufficient eligible dialogue and topic context.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Argument analysis.
steps: System loads the authorized dialogue and topic with speaker/turn attribution.
Argument Coach identifies main claims, reasons, counterarguments, concessions and rebuttal links.
System validates structured output and invokes UC-06-05 for every quoted critique.
System displays a context-linked argument map and explanations of relevance, evidence use and unanswered points, each paired with a concrete repair.
use_cases.success: Argument findings are attributable to the dialogue and offer specific reasoning improvements.
use_cases.minimum: Grammar, accent and personal traits never substitute for argument-quality evidence.
use_cases.special: A rebuttal assessment must identify the opponent point and the learner response, not simply label a speaker weak. Detailed analysis belongs after the debate.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, transcript is incomplete or speech is insufficient.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, transcript is incomplete or speech is insufficient.
alternatives.outcome: Label the analysis partial/unavailable and avoid declaring an opponent point definitively unanswered without the needed context.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2 or 3, provider/schema/evidence validation fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 2 or 3, provider/schema/evidence validation fails.
alternatives.outcome: Repair once where specified, discard invalid findings and show the section status.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 4, evidence supports multiple interpretations.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, evidence supports multiple interpretations.
alternatives.outcome: Describe the uncertainty and show surrounding turns rather than assigning hidden motives.

alternatives.label: A3 — At step 4, optional fallacy analysis is requested.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, optional fallacy analysis is requested.
alternatives.outcome: Open UC-07-02 only when enabled; basic argument review remains usable.

use_cases.title: Review potential logical fallacies
use_cases.preconditions: Optional fallacy analysis is enabled and the learner can access eligible argument context.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Potential logical fallacies.
steps: System selects a candidate reasoning pattern with speaker and surrounding turn context.
Argument Coach proposes a potential fallacy label, exact quote and explanation of the reasoning failure.
System invokes UC-06-05 and checks that the explanation is supported by the cited context.
System displays the potential label, transcript link and a concrete reformulation/remediation.
use_cases.success: Any visible fallacy finding is qualified, evidenced and paired with a reasoning repair.
use_cases.minimum: No personal attack, motive attribution or ungrounded accusation is displayed.
use_cases.special: Use potential when interpretation is uncertain. Ad hominem/strawman/false-dilemma labels need actual reasoning context, not isolated wording.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, no defensible pattern is found.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, no defensible pattern is found.
alternatives.outcome: Show no retained fallacy findings without inventing a label or falsely praising the entire argument.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, quote fails provenance or context does not justify the label.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, quote fails provenance or context does not justify the label.
alternatives.outcome: Suppress the finding; do not accuse the learner based on a keyword alone.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 2, provider fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, provider fails.
alternatives.outcome: Mark optional analysis unavailable while preserving the core argument review.

use_cases.title: Inspect claim verdicts and evidence
use_cases.preconditions: Learner can access a debate with selected attributable factual claims; fact-checking is enabled.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Claim evidence.
steps: System ranks check-worthy factual claims, selects within the default eight-claim budget and shows which claims were checked.
SearchAdapter retrieves bounded source snippets for the selected claim; system sanitizes and de-duplicates external content.
Evidence Evaluator and Skeptic independently assess the same evidence and produce schema-valid five-way verdicts.
Deterministic rules preserve disagreement as Contested; system displays the verdict, uncertainty, source links and exact supporting snippets.
Learner inspects sources and the scope/limitations of the evidence search.
use_cases.success: Selected claims have inspectable evidence/limitations and transparent verdict disagreement.
use_cases.minimum: Search failure or model agreement never becomes proof of absolute truth.
use_cases.special: External text is untrusted data, never instructions. Default limits: top eight claims, up to five results/query, snippets truncated to 1,000 characters. Exact snippet quotes and provenance remain visible.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, claim is opinion, prediction, vague or below selection budget/rank.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, claim is opinion, prediction, vague or below selection budget/rank.
alternatives.outcome: Label Not verifiable or Not selected as appropriate; do not imply unchecked claims are true.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, no reliable source is found or search fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, no reliable source is found or search fails.
alternatives.outcome: Show Insufficient evidence/no sources found or unavailable stage, not a source-free certainty claim.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, evaluators disagree.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, evaluators disagree.
alternatives.outcome: Show both assessments and Contested rather than hiding the weaker/contradictory result.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, schema/provider output remains invalid after the allowed repair.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, schema/provider output remains invalid after the allowed repair.
alternatives.outcome: Mark that stage unavailable and keep any valid evidence explicitly partial.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 5, a source link is unavailable or content changed.
alternatives.detail: At step 5, a source link is unavailable or content changed.
alternatives.outcome: Retain the cited snippet/retrieval context with a limitation; do not claim a fresh verification.

use_cases.title: Show optional live fact-check overlay
use_cases.preconditions: Optional live overlay is enabled and learner is in a consented LIVE audio session.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opts into live fact-check overlays.
steps: System explains the optional overlay, bounded claim selection and uncertain results.
Learner enables it; system processes eligible final turns asynchronously under the claim budget.
System shows a compact nonblocking evidence/status card only when a valid result exists.
Learner expands the evidence or hides the overlay while audio/end controls remain accessible.
use_cases.success: Optional compact cards expose evidence without disrupting the debate.
use_cases.minimum: Overlay availability never becomes a prerequisite for speaking or ending.
use_cases.special: Stretch extension of UC-04-02. Keep critical feedback post-debate by default and avoid repeated alerts during socially intense discussion.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, learner declines or hides the overlay.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, learner declines or hides the overlay.
alternatives.outcome: Continue the audio debate without live cards; post-debate evidence review remains available.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, processing is slow, rate limited or fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, processing is slow, rate limited or fails.
alternatives.outcome: Delay/drop optional cards and show unavailable status; never buffer or pause audio for fact checking.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, evaluators disagree or evidence is absent.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, evaluators disagree or evidence is absent.
alternatives.outcome: Show Contested/insufficient evidence, not a confident live accusation.

use_cases.title: Review debate evaluation and consensus
use_cases.preconditions: Learner may access an ended debate and its available versioned analysis inputs.
