use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Evaluation and consensus.
steps: System loads the versioned debate rubric and the available argument/evidence summaries.

Debate Judge produces six schema-valid 0–100 dimension scores per speaker: ArgumentQuality, Relevance, Evidence, Reasoning, Rebuttal and Counterarguments, with quoted/contextual rationales and qualitative fallacy/clarity notes.
Deterministic consensus validates score ranges, records available evaluators and flags relevant disagreement.
System displays dimension explanations, uncertainty and the honest single-evaluator baseline alongside source findings.
use_cases.success: Learner can inspect a qualified, versioned evaluation and its agreement limits.
use_cases.minimum: A score is never presented as certified proficiency or an undisputed factual verdict.
use_cases.special: Architecture Section 11.3 defines six numeric dimensions per speaker—ArgumentQuality, Relevance, Evidence, Reasoning, Rebuttal and Counterarguments—each 0–100; fallacy/clarity notes remain qualitative. Both speakers therefore have twelve numeric values in a complete evaluation. MVP uses one debate judge and self-reported confidence at most 0.8; claim Evaluator/Skeptic disagreement is separate from debate-score consensus.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, inputs are missing or speech is insufficient.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, inputs are missing or speech is insufficient.
alternatives.outcome: Label evaluation partial/unavailable and do not assign a fabricated overall zero or winner.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, schema/range validation fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, schema/range validation fails.
alternatives.outcome: Use the defined one repair attempt, then mark that stage failed.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, a future multi-judge score spread exceeds 15/100.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, a future multi-judge score spread exceeds 15/100.
alternatives.outcome: Flag Contested and show the disagreement; do not silently average it away.

alternatives.label: A3 — At step 4, submitted human grades have current dual sharing permission.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, submitted human grades have current dual sharing permission.
alternatives.outcome: Offer UC-09-06 beside AI evaluation without overwriting either result.

use_cases.title: Configure analysis and inspect usage
use_cases.preconditions: Admin is authenticated with configuration/usage permission; versioned settings exist.
use_cases.trigger: Admin opens Analysis settings or Usage.
steps: System loads nonsecret provider/model identifiers, prompt/rubric versions, flags, evaluator count and budget settings.
Admin reviews aggregated usage/cost estimates and edits permitted settings.
System validates supported combinations, limits and feature scope and asks confirmation for an impactful change.
System saves a versioned configuration and shows which future jobs use it; existing results keep their recorded versions.
use_cases.success: Authorized settings are versioned and usage is inspectable without secret disclosure.
use_cases.minimum: Failed configuration writes do not change the active valid settings or historical rubric provenance.
use_cases.special: API keys belong only in server-side environment/secret management, never browser fields or screenshots. Configuring a feature cannot bypass consent or approve a deferred capability.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, admin only inspects usage or cancels editing.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, admin only inspects usage or cancels editing.
alternatives.outcome: Leave settings unchanged and distinguish estimates from measured token usage.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, provider/model/limit combination is invalid.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, provider/model/limit combination is invalid.
alternatives.outcome: Reject the change with field guidance; retain the last valid configuration.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 1 or 4, role is invalid or a concurrent save/failure occurs.
alternatives.detail: At step 1 or 4, role is invalid or a concurrent save/failure occurs.
alternatives.outcome: Deny or reload/reconcile the current version; do not announce an unconfirmed rollout.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 2, usage data is incomplete.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, usage data is incomplete.
alternatives.outcome: Show missing periods/unknown costs rather than fabricated totals.

use_cases.title: Run optional heterogeneous judge panel
use_cases.preconditions: Stretch panel feature is approved; Admin has permission and a reviewed multi-model budget/consensus policy.
use_cases.trigger: Admin chooses a heterogeneous judge panel for an eligible ended debate.
steps: Admin selects at least three different supported judge models and a bounded budget.
System validates feature approval, model diversity, schemas and available quota.
System runs independent versioned judgments on the same eligible summaries.
Deterministic aggregation displays per-model outcomes, score spread, confidence policy and Contested status where required.
use_cases.success: A reviewed optional panel produces transparent per-model and aggregate results.
use_cases.minimum: Incomplete panels never masquerade as three independent completed judges.
use_cases.special: Not the MVP default; approval and provider configuration are prerequisites. Different prompts to one model do not meet the heterogeneous-model requirement.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2, fewer than three distinct models or unsupported configuration is selected.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, fewer than three distinct models or unsupported configuration is selected.
alternatives.outcome: Reject panel activation and preserve the baseline setting.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, a provider fails or budget is exhausted.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, a provider fails or budget is exhausted.
alternatives.outcome: Stop bounded work, expose the actual completed panel size and label the result partial.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 4, scores differ by more than 15/100.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, scores differ by more than 15/100.
alternatives.outcome: Mark Contested and show individual scores instead of claiming consensus.

use_cases.title: Assign a human evaluator
use_cases.preconditions: Creator is a debater in an ENDED room; conditional human evaluation is enabled.
use_cases.trigger: Creator requests assignment of a human evaluator.
steps: Creator selects an eligible human evaluator for the finished debate.
System explains transcript/grade sharing and obtains explicit current approval from both debaters.
System verifies ENDED, creator authority, both grants and evaluator eligibility.
System records the assignment and grants that evaluator access only to this debate and the versioned grading card.
use_cases.success: A named evaluator is assigned only under current dual sharing authorization for an ended debate.
use_cases.minimum: No assignment preview leaks transcripts before both debaters agree.
use_cases.special: Evaluator is a separate role from Admin. Record assignment and consent provenance; this use case does not create classes or give global learner access.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, either debater declines or has not approved.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, either debater declines or has not approved.
alternatives.outcome: Keep assignment inactive; evaluator receives no transcript or grade access.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, room is LIVE, caller is not creator or evaluator is ineligible.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, room is LIVE, caller is not creator or evaluator is ineligible.
alternatives.outcome: Reject assignment without exposing private content.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, save fails or a sharing grant is revoked.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, save fails or a sharing grant is revoked.
alternatives.outcome: Keep access disabled/revoke it promptly and reconcile the assignment before retry.

use_cases.title: Submit human grading card
use_cases.preconditions: Human evaluator is authenticated, assigned to this ENDED debate and sharing grants remain valid.
use_cases.trigger: Evaluator opens the assigned grading card.
steps: System rechecks assignment, ended state and current sharing grants before loading the permitted transcript.
System displays the versioned card with the Debate Judge's six 0–100 dimensions for each speaker: ArgumentQuality, Relevance, Evidence, Reasoning, Rebuttal and Counterarguments.
Evaluator enters all twelve numeric values, adds evidence-based comments and qualitative fallacy/clarity notes, and explicitly submits.
System validates and stores the human grade separately, recording evaluator, timestamp, card version and rubric version.
use_cases.success: A complete attributable human grade is submitted separately from AI evaluation.
use_cases.minimum: No unauthorized grade, draft disclosure or overwrite of AI scores occurs.
use_cases.special: All six dimensions from Architecture Section 11.3 are required for each speaker, with individual values in 0–100; fallacy/clarity notes are qualitative rather than additional numeric dimensions. Rubric/card versions and evaluator identity remain visible to authorized debaters. Submit is explicit; drafting never implies publication.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 3, evaluator saves no submission or leaves the card.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, evaluator saves no submission or leaves the card.
alternatives.outcome: Keep any unsubmitted work private; debaters see no draft grade.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1 or 4, assignment/consent was revoked or room is not ENDED.
alternatives.detail: At step 1 or 4, assignment/consent was revoked or room is not ENDED.
alternatives.outcome: Deny read/write access and expose no transcript or draft grade.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, required dimensions or score ranges are invalid.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, required dimensions or score ranges are invalid.
alternatives.outcome: Show field errors and do not publish a partial grading card.

alternatives.label: E3 — At step 4, response is lost or submission repeats.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, response is lost or submission repeats.
alternatives.outcome: Reconcile the existing submission identity rather than creating duplicate grades.

use_cases.title: View shared human grades
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is a debater in the ended room; a human grade was submitted and both sharing grants remain valid.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Human grade from the evaluation view.
steps: System checks debate membership, submitted status and current dual sharing consent.
System loads the human grade with evaluator identity, submission time and card/rubric versions.
System displays human and AI evaluations side by side with their separate provenance.
Learner inspects dimension comments and supporting permitted transcript context.
use_cases.success: Authorized learners see only submitted, currently shared human grades beside independent AI results.
use_cases.minimum: No draft or revoked human grade becomes visible.
use_cases.special: Extension of UC-09-01; human grading is not required for the core AI evaluation view to work.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, grading is assigned but not submitted.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, grading is assigned but not submitted.
alternatives.outcome: Show Awaiting submission without exposing scores or comments from drafts.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1 or 4, either sharing grant is revoked or membership is unauthorized.
alternatives.detail: At step 1 or 4, either sharing grant is revoked or membership is unauthorized.
alternatives.outcome: Hide the human-grade content and deny further retrieval.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, human and AI scores differ.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, human and AI scores differ.
alternatives.outcome: Show both with their distinct rationale/versions; do not silently replace one with an average.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 2, retrieval fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, retrieval fails.
alternatives.outcome: Show unavailable/retry without leaking cached grades to an unauthorized session.

use_cases.title: Review personalized learning report
use_cases.preconditions: Learner can access their ended debate and the available transcript/analysis stages.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Learning report.
steps: System checks participation and loads stage statuses plus the learner own eligible findings.
System combines available summary, language metrics, argument findings, claim evidence and evaluation with explicit section provenance.
Learning Coach proposes a short CEFR-appropriate practice plan whose recommendations refer to grounded examples.
System displays the report with priority actions, transcript links and any incomplete/unavailable sections.
use_cases.success: Learner sees an honest personalized report with evidence-linked, actionable practice.
use_cases.minimum: A partial report never appears complete and private opponent details are not included beyond the authorized shared debate context.
use_cases.special: Report generation is post-debate and asynchronous. Clinical critique requires a precise repair; do not give participation-trophy praise or certified CEFR advancement claims.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, processing is queued/running.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, processing is queued/running.
alternatives.outcome: Show real stage progress and only completed sections; offer UC-10-04 when appropriate.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 2 or 3, a provider/stage fails or evidence is insufficient.
alternatives.detail: At step 2 or 3, a provider/stage fails or evidence is insufficient.
alternatives.outcome: Publish a clearly partial report or insufficient-speech explanation; never invent missing findings/scores.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3, a practice recommendation has no valid supporting evidence.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, a practice recommendation has no valid supporting evidence.
alternatives.outcome: Discard/revise the recommendation rather than fabricating learner weaknesses.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 4, optional PDF export is requested.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, optional PDF export is requested.
alternatives.outcome: Invoke UC-10-05 only if enabled and authorized.

use_cases.title: Browse own debate history
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens My debates.
steps: System retrieves only the learner participant-scoped debate history.
System lists topic, date, session state and report availability using stable pagination.
Learner selects a debate and chooses its report or transcript.
System rechecks resource access and opens the selected authorized detail view.
use_cases.success: Learner navigates only their authorized prior debate records.
use_cases.minimum: History and detail queries cannot be widened by changing a supplied user or debate ID.
use_cases.special: No public leaderboard, opponent profile browsing or teacher access is implied. Empty history remains empty until actual sessions exist.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, learner has no debates.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, learner has no debates.
alternatives.outcome: Show an empty state and a path to topic/room creation rather than example personal history.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 2, a debate has incomplete analysis.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, a debate has incomplete analysis.
alternatives.outcome: Show processing/partial status; opening it follows UC-10-04/UC-10-01.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 4, debate was deleted or access changed.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, debate was deleted or access changed.
alternatives.outcome: Remove the stale entry/show unavailable without exposing content.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 1 or 2, history loading fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 1 or 2, history loading fails.
alternatives.outcome: Preserve the selected position/filter and offer retry; do not show stale history as current.

use_cases.title: Review longitudinal progress
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated; longitudinal analysis is enabled and eligible own history exists.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens Progress and selects a time range.
steps: System selects own eligible reports and checks metric/rubric versions for comparability.
System aggregates observed score/metric trends and recurring grounded patterns.
System plots dated observations with sample counts, missing periods and version boundaries.
Learner opens a point/pattern to inspect the underlying debate evidence and chooses a practice focus.
use_cases.success: Learner can inspect measured historical patterns and their evidence limits.
use_cases.minimum: No trend certifies proficiency gains or infers nonexistent past performance.
use_cases.special: Privacy/deletion rules apply to aggregates too. Missing/failed reports are gaps, not zero scores; avoid implying statistical certainty from small samples.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, too few comparable observations exist.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, too few comparable observations exist.
alternatives.outcome: Show available sessions and Not enough comparable data; draw no fabricated trend.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 2, rubric/metric versions changed.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, rubric/metric versions changed.
alternatives.outcome: Separate series or label a comparison boundary; do not connect incompatible scores as continuous improvement.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 4, source data was deleted or a finding invalidated.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, source data was deleted or a finding invalidated.
alternatives.outcome: Recompute/remove affected observations and explain gaps.

use_cases.title: Track analysis status and retry
use_cases.preconditions: Learner is authenticated and authorized for the ended debate report.
use_cases.trigger: Learner opens analysis status or selects Retry failed stages.
steps: System loads actual queued, running, completed and failed stage records with permitted progress detail.
System marks the report partial and identifies retryable failed stages without exposing provider traces.
Learner requests a retry; server rechecks permission, current job state and remaining attempt/budget limits.
System enqueues only permitted failed work, preserves valid completed results and updates status until completion/failure.
use_cases.success: A bounded retry has an actual job/status and completed valid results remain available.
use_cases.minimum: Repeated clicks cannot create unbounded provider calls or turn an incomplete report into a fake success.
use_cases.special: Stage retry policy and usage are server-controlled. Deletion wins over regeneration; never recreate erased learner data from stale jobs.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 1, all stages completed.
alternatives.detail: At step 1, all stages completed.
alternatives.outcome: Open the complete report and do not create another job.

alternatives.label: A2 — At step 3, a retry is already queued/running or request repeats.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, a retry is already queued/running or request repeats.
alternatives.outcome: Return the existing job/status rather than duplicate costly work.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 3, retry is exhausted, rate limited or provider remains unavailable.
alternatives.detail: At step 3, retry is exhausted, rate limited or provider remains unavailable.
alternatives.outcome: Explain the bounded retry state and preserve the labelled partial report.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 4, enqueue fails or source data was deleted.
alternatives.detail: At step 4, enqueue fails or source data was deleted.
alternatives.outcome: Keep the old valid sections, show the failed retry accurately and do not claim regeneration completed.

use_cases.title: Export report PDF
use_cases.preconditions: Learner can access a report; optional report-PDF export has been implemented.
use_cases.trigger: Learner selects Export PDF from report review.
steps: System rechecks report ownership/membership and loads the selected report version.
System displays which sections and limitations will be included, with any partial status retained.
Learner confirms export; system creates the authorized PDF with evidence links and version/date context.
System starts the download without creating a public sharing link.
use_cases.success: An authorized local PDF preserves report provenance and limitations.
use_cases.minimum: No export leaks secrets, unshared human grades or unrelated opponent data.
use_cases.special: Stretch product feature; distinct from compiling PA3 submission documents with latexmk. A local download is not consent to publish the report.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, report is partial.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, report is partial.
alternatives.outcome: Offer a clearly labelled partial export or wait; never title it complete.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1 or 3, access was revoked or data deleted.
alternatives.detail: At step 1 or 3, access was revoked or data deleted.
alternatives.outcome: Cancel export and deliver no report bytes.

alternatives.label: E2 — At step 3 or 4, rendering/download fails.
alternatives.detail: At step 3 or 4, rendering/download fails.
alternatives.outcome: Show retryable export failure; the saved report stays unchanged.

use_cases.title: Process deletion and retention requests
use_cases.preconditions: Admin has deletion/retention permission and an authorized request or due retention record exists.
use_cases.trigger: Admin opens the deletion queue or a retention item becomes due.
steps: System verifies request provenance, affected identity and applicable retention/deletion policy.
Admin reviews the scoped records and confirms the authorized erasure/policy action.
System disables affected access and schedules/removes transcript, analysis, report, derived aggregates and optional chat according to the request.
System verifies progress, records noncontent audit status and shows completed or outstanding deletion work.
use_cases.success: Authorized erasure/retention is applied with verifiable completion or explicit outstanding work.
use_cases.minimum: A deletion failure never restores access or silently leaves derived private artifacts visible.
use_cases.special: Default transcript retention is 90 days and user-configurable; accepted account hard deletion is due within seven days. Audit status must not retain erased transcript/quote contents.

alternatives.label: A1 — At step 2, admin cancels a not-yet-accepted manual action.
alternatives.detail: At step 2, admin cancels a not-yet-accepted manual action.
alternatives.outcome: Do not widen erasure scope; an existing accepted account-deletion deadline still applies.

alternatives.label: E1 — At step 1, requester/role/scope is invalid.

use_cases.title: View consented student dashboards
use_cases.preconditions: Post-MVP dashboard sharing is separately approved; student already joined a class and authenticated Teacher has an existing relationship.
use_cases.trigger: Student chooses dashboard sharing or Teacher opens a consented student dashboard.
steps: Student reviews the read-only sharing scope and explicitly grants or revokes dashboard access.
System verifies the existing relationship and current student sharing decision for each Teacher request.
System shows only the allowed dashboard/report summary in a read-only view with student identity and sharing status.
Student can revoke access at any time; system blocks subsequent reads and clears the Teacher view on refresh/update.
use_cases.success: Only a currently authorized Teacher can read the explicitly shared existing dashboard.
use_cases.minimum: No class membership alone exposes student learning data and no write authority is granted.
